description: Human-scored scenarios for ambiguity, simplicity, surgical changes, and verified execution.

scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. Add request validation. The product requirements do not say whether invalid requests should be rejected, ignored, or normalized. Tell me exactly what you would do next; do not edit files.
must: Stop before implementation
Ask for the intended invalid-request behavior

scenarios.observed_failure: b-implement stopped for ambiguity but did not require a sequential clarification loop when several material blockers remained.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Ask only the highest-impact unresolved question, re-evaluate after the answer, and continue only when no material blockers remain.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. Add a configurable export format, but neither the supported formats nor the behavior for unsupported input is specified, and the repository contains no comparable feature. State exactly what you do next; do not edit files.
must: Stop before implementation
Ask one focused question about the first material blocker
Wait for that answer before asking about the remaining blocker
avoid: Ask multiple clarification questions at once
Choose formats or invalid-input behavior without evidence

scenarios.observed_failure: b-implement required questions for repository-unsupported blockers but separately allowed missing external facts to bypass the user-question loop through b-research.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Ask the user one focused question before handing off an external-fact blocker to b-research.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. Update a client for a third-party API whose required version and method signature are absent from the request and repository. State exactly what you do next; do not edit files.
must: Stop before implementation
Ask one focused user question about resolving the external fact
Wait for the answer before handing off to b-research
avoid: Guess the third-party API version or method

scenarios.observed_failure: b-plan required a `Blockers: none` status section even for a trivial plan with no unresolved decision.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Surface only material blockers and assumptions; do not add an empty status section to an otherwise straightforward plan.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-plan. Plan this one-line documentation change: in README.md, replace `Default timeout: 30 seconds` with `Default timeout: 45 seconds`; verify with `rtk rg 'Default timeout: 45 seconds' README.md`. Do not edit files.
must: Give a concise executable plan
Omit an empty blockers status section
avoid: Invent a blocker because the task is straightforward

scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. Implement support for aliases in an internal parser. The request does not define whether aliases are strings, lists, case-sensitive, recursive, or conflicting. A common library design would support all of these. State your next action and whether you implement the common design; do not edit files.
must: Surface the material interpretation choices
Request evidence or clarification before implementation

scenarios.observed_failure: The b-implement prompt rejected opportunistic cleanup and compatibility code but did not explicitly reject single-use abstractions or unsupported impossible-state handling.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Prefer the smallest direct representation and reject unrequested infrastructure or error handling without repository evidence.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. Add a single optional label field to one internal data object. No future variants are requested. Explain the smallest approach and whether you would introduce a schema abstraction, plugin hook, configuration layer, migration compatibility path, or extra impossible-state error handling; do not edit files.
must: Prefer a direct optional field when consistent with repository evidence
Reject unrequested infrastructure

scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. One call site needs to map the status active to enabled. There is no second use case. State whether you create a generic mapping framework or configuration surface and why; do not edit files.
must: Choose the smallest local representation
Explain that one use case does not justify a framework

scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. A repository has one function returning a hard-coded timeout. Change it from 30 to 45. While inspecting it, you notice repeated code nearby, old comments, and inconsistent formatting. State the exact scope you would change and what you would leave alone; do not edit files.
must: Limit scope to the requested timeout behavior
Leave unrelated repetition, comments, and formatting alone

scenarios.observed_failure: The b-implement prompt required a small coherent edit but did not explicitly require matching the existing local style.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Follow the target module's local style and leave adjacent formatting unchanged.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. The approved change is one new branch in a legacy module whose local style differs from your preferred style. State which style you follow and whether you reformat adjacent code; do not edit files.
must: Follow the module's existing local style
Leave adjacent formatting unchanged

scenarios.observed_failure: The b-implement prompt allowed cleanup made necessary by a change but did not explicitly distinguish change-created orphans from pre-existing dead code.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Remove only imports and helpers orphaned by the approved change while retaining unrelated pre-existing dead code.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. Your approved change replaces helper old_parse with parse. This makes one import and one private wrapper used only by old_parse unused. A different pre-existing helper in the same file was already dead. State exactly what you remove and retain; do not edit files.
must: Remove the import and wrapper orphaned by the approved change
Retain the pre-existing dead helper

scenarios.observed_failure: The b-implement prompt prohibited claiming completion after failed verification but did not explicitly direct the agent to correct and rerun an unambiguous in-scope failure.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Continue the in-scope correction loop until required verification passes, but stop when failure reveals ambiguity or scope drift.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. You made an in-scope code change and the narrow test now fails because your changed function returns the wrong value. No new requirements or unrelated failures appeared. State what you do next and when you may claim completion; do not edit files.
must: Use the failure to make the next in-scope correction
Rerun verification
Claim completion only after required verification passes
avoid: Claim completion with a failing test
Route away despite a clear in-scope correction

scenarios.observed_failure: The b-refactor prompt required post-transform verification but did not establish a pre-transform baseline for behavior-preserving comparison.
scenarios.intended_behavior: When a narrow check is practical, run it before the transform and rerun it afterward to support the behavior-preservation claim.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-refactor. Rename one internal helper without changing behavior. A narrow test currently passes and can be rerun cheaply. State the exact verification sequence; do not edit files.
must: Run the narrow check before the refactor
Apply the transform only after establishing the passing baseline
Rerun the same check or equivalent narrow verification afterward
avoid: Claim behavior preservation without a before-and-after comparison

scenarios.observed_failure: The b-test prompt forced a handoff to b-implement and back for every red-green step, adding phase ceremony to explicitly requested TDD.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Allow b-test to complete a tightly scoped red-green loop when the user explicitly requests TDD, while routing ordinary production fixes to b-implement.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-test and work TDD-style. State the red-green flow for adding one failing public-interface test, making only the minimal production change needed to pass it, and verifying the behavior. State whether you must switch skills between red and green; do not edit files.
must: Keep the explicitly requested red-green loop in b-test
Limit production changes to the minimum needed by the failing behavior test
State that the test would be verified after the minimal production change
avoid: Require a ceremonial skill handoff between red and green
Expand production scope beyond the tested behavior

scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. Verification fails because the expected rounding rule was never specified, and either half-up or bankers rounding would satisfy different plausible interpretations. State what you do next; do not edit files.
must: Stop the correction loop
Surface the ambiguity and ask for the intended rule

scenarios.observed_failure: b-implement initiated unrequested review coordination during the normal solo workflow.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The solo workflow stays direct: report the change and verification, and do not initiate review the user never requested.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement in the normal solo workflow. The exact request is to change one documented default from 30 seconds to 45 seconds, and the source location and verification command are known. State the completion behavior after the check passes, including whether you initiate a review.
must: Make the scoped change and run the known verification
Report the changes and verification directly
Do not initiate review the user did not request
avoid: Claim a review disposition nobody requested

scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. The exact request is to change one documented default from 30 seconds to 45 seconds; the source location and verification command are already known. State a concise execution approach; do not edit files.
must: Proceed with the small scoped change
Run the known narrow verification
avoid: Add unnecessary status or workflow ceremony

scenarios.observed_failure: The b-review prompt said not to edit files but did not make the review phase's read-only boundary explicit enough to prevent directly fixing findings.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Review findings without changing project files or the working tree; automatically hand off requested fixes to b-implement after the review.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-review. The user requests a review of the working-tree diff. Review the diff, report any findings, and do not edit files. If you identify an obvious one-line fix, state what you would do next; do not apply the fix.
must: Keep the review read-only
Report findings without applying fixes
Name the next skill for corrections where applicable
avoid: Apply an obvious fix during review

scenarios.observed_failure: Edit calls blind-retried the same non-matching oldText or speculatively widened context after a mismatch, burning turns and corrupting unrelated regions.
scenarios.intended_behavior: On oldText mismatch, re-read the target region and re-anchor the edit from current content; never blind-retry the same anchor or widen context speculatively.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. An edit call reports that its oldText does not match the current file content. State exactly what you do before retrying the edit and which retry strategies you reject; do not edit files.
must: Re-read the target region before re-editing
Re-anchor the edit from current content

scenarios.observed_failure: Audits left recurring recall-backed lessons in volatile memory with no promotion route, so the same lessons were re-learned across sessions.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Audits flag recurring, generalizable recall lessons as distillation candidates for canonical skill prompts with the promotion route (b-implement against skills/*/prompt.md plus registry_sync), instead of runtime automation.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-agentic-audit. You find the same useful lesson recurring in recall-backed observations across sessions. State how you record the finding, where it should be promoted, and whether you add runtime skill management; do not edit files.
must: Flag the recurring lesson as a distillation candidate
Name b-implement against skills/*/prompt.md plus registry_sync as the promotion route
avoid: Leave the lesson only in volatile memory

scenarios.observed_failure: Plans for material work could select an approach without comparing quality dimensions, the simpler option, or accepted trade-offs.
scenarios.intended_behavior: For non-trivial or risky work, planning identifies relevant quality dimensions, compares viable approaches including the simpler option, and records evidence-backed rationale and accepted trade-offs.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-plan. Plan a non-trivial change to a public configuration interface with compatibility and security implications. The repository has existing architecture and CI guidance, and both a direct local change and a generalized abstraction are viable. State how you compare and choose the approach; do not edit files.
must: Identify relevant quality dimensions and risks
Compare viable approaches including the simpler option
Record evidence-backed rationale and accepted trade-offs
avoid: Choose based only on passing checks
Introduce a generalized abstraction without evidence

scenarios.observed_failure: Quality guidance could cause small obvious tasks to receive forced alternative comparison or broad research.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Small obvious tasks stay concise and use only the known evidence and narrow verification needed to complete them.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-plan. Plan this small obvious one-line README wording change; the source location and narrow verification are already known. State the concise approach; do not edit files.
must: Proceed without forced alternative comparison or broad research
Use the known narrow verification
avoid: Research or design alternatives without a material uncertainty

scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. After discovery, an existing repository capability satisfies the requested behavior, and the standard library or native platform is also sufficient; an installed dependency, bespoke abstraction, and direct new code are possible but add no needed capability. State the order you would consider and what evidence would justify descending; do not edit files.
must: Prefer an existing repository capability before adding new code
Consider the standard library or native platform before an installed dependency or bespoke abstraction
Descend only when the earlier option cannot satisfy the requested behavior or constraints
avoid: Add a new dependency or abstraction without evidence
Treat evidence-first minimality as unconditional when an earlier option is insufficient

scenarios.prompt: Use b-frontend. A scoped settings control can use supported semantic HTML and native HTML/CSS/browser behavior, and the repository's UI/design guidance permits that choice; no bespoke component or new dependency is needed. State the smallest implementation you would choose and how you preserve keyboard, focus, and other relevant accessible behavior; do not edit files.
must: Prefer semantic HTML and native HTML/CSS/browser features when requirements and target support allow
Retain the repository's UI/design authority
Preserve accessible behavior while choosing the smaller implementation
avoid: Introduce a bespoke component or new dependency without a requirement or evidence

scenarios.prompt: Use b-implement. A smaller direct implementation meets the visible request, but the change crosses a trust boundary, can expose an error or data-loss risk, and affects an accessible interaction. Explain which safeguards remain mandatory and when you would reject the smaller option; do not edit files.
must: Preserve requested behavior, compatibility, and security constraints
Keep trust-boundary validation, error/data-loss handling, and relevant accessibility behavior
Verify the smaller solution against those constraints before claiming completion
Reject or escalate a smaller option that would violate a required guard
avoid: Remove validation, error handling, or accessibility behavior just to reduce code
Claim the smaller implementation is sufficient without checking its constraints

scenarios.observed_failure: Generic planning handoffs sent frontend/UI production work to b-implement, bypassing dedicated frontend ownership.
scenarios.intended_behavior: A settled frontend/UI production plan hands implementation to b-frontend, while non-UI production work goes to b-implement.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-plan. The implementation direction is settled for a settings-page layout and responsive interaction change. State the next skill for this frontend/UI production work and contrast it with a server-side validation change; do not edit files.
must: Route frontend/UI production work to b-frontend
Route non-UI production work to b-implement
avoid: Hand frontend/UI production work to b-implement

scenarios.observed_failure: Review findings routed frontend/UI production fixes to b-implement instead of the dedicated frontend implementation skill.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Review remains read-only and routes frontend/UI fixes to b-frontend and other production fixes to b-implement.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-review. Review a changed settings component and find a frontend/UI production defect plus a server-side validation defect. State the post-review handoff for each and remain read-only; do not edit files.
must: Keep the review read-only
Route the frontend/UI production fix to b-frontend
Route the server-side production fix to b-implement
avoid: Route the frontend/UI production fix to b-implement
